indication_tracked: Itovebi, in combination with palbociclib and fulvestrant, is indicated for the treatment of adult patients with PIK3CA-mutated, oestrogen receptor (ER)-positive, HER2-negative, locally advanced or metastatic breast cancer, following recurrence on or within 12 months of completing adjuvant endocrine treatment (see section 5.1). Patients previously treated with a CDK 4/6 inhibitor in the (neo)adjuvant setting should have had an interval of at least 12 months between termination of CDK 4/6 inhibitor treatment and the detection of recurrence. In pre/perimenopausal women and in men, endocrine therapy should be combined with a luteinising hormone releasing hormone (LHRH) agonist.
indication_source: Therapeutic indication as published in EMA's medicines data (word for word)

eu.epar_summary:
Itovebi is a medicine used in combination with two other medicines (palbociclib and fulvestrant) to treat breast cancer when the cancer cells are ER positive and HER2-negative and have a mutation in a gene called PIK3CA. ER-positive means that cancer cells have receptors for oestrogen hormones on their surface and HER2-negative means that they do not have large quantities of a receptor called HER2.

Itovebi is used for cancer that is locally advanced (has spread nearby) or metastatic (has spread to other parts of the body) when the cancer has come back during or within 12 months of adjuvant hormonal treatment. An adjuvant treatment is an additional treatment given after the main treatment to lower the risk of cancer coming back.

Patients previously given a type of cancer medicine called CDK 4/6 inhibitor can be given Itovebi, in combination with palbociclib and fulvestrant, only if the cancer has come back after at least 12 months since stopping treatment with the CDK 4/6 inhibitor.

Women who have not yet reached the menopause (pre-menopausal or perimenopausal) and men should also be given a luteinising hormone-releasing hormone (LHRH) agonist (a medicine that lowers blood levels of the hormones oestrogen and progesterone).

Itovebi contains the active substance inavolisib.

DE.outcome_short: Indication of considerable added benefit (women without prior CDK4/6 inhibitor)
DE.opinion: a1) Women not treated before with a CDK4/6 inhibitor in the (neo)adjuvant setting: indication (Anhaltspunkt) of a considerable added benefit (overall survival advantage; more treatment stops due to side effects). a2) Women treated before with a CDK4/6 inhibitor: added benefit not proven. b) Men: added benefit not proven.
DE.comparator: a) Endocrine therapy options: tamoxifen, letrozole, exemestane, anastrozole, fulvestrant, everolimus + exemestane, or a CDK4/6 inhibitor (ribociclib, abemaciclib, palbociclib) with an aromatase inhibitor or fulvestrant; b) tamoxifen or palbociclib + an aromatase inhibitor. The trial compared inavolisib + palbociclib + fulvestrant with palbociclib + fulvestrant.
DE.reimbursement: Reimbursed by statutory health insurance (GKV); price negotiated with GKV-Spitzenverband after the G-BA decision.

price.type: Annual therapy cost in the G-BA decision; with palbociclib and fulvestrant €217,654.49 (after statutory discounts, Lauer-Taxe 15 Dec 2025)

FR.opinion: SMR important in the indication of the marketing authorisation. ASMR IV (minor clinical added value) versus palbociclib + fulvestrant, based on longer progression-free and overall survival; HAS noted that palbociclib is a debatable comparator, that no gain in quality of life was shown, and that serious side effects (including high blood sugar) were more frequent.
FR.reimbursement: Opinion for initial listing (inscription). Marketed in France (declared 8 Jan 2026); no reimbursement rate or price in BDPM yet.

price.note: No price in BDPM yet. Checked in the French public medicines database (BDPM) on 22 Nov 2026.

IT.reimbursement: Reimbursed by the national health service (class A or H). The exact class and conditions are in the determina on TrovaNormeFarmaco.

price.note: Not yet in AIFA's public class A/H lists (latest list 30 Jun 2026 is older than this decision).

eligibility_plain: Adults with advanced or metastatic breast cancer that is hormone receptor (ER) positive, HER2 negative and has a PIK3CA gene change, when the cancer came back during or within 12 months after finishing hormone therapy given after surgery. It is taken together with palbociclib and fulvestrant. A tumour test for PIK3CA is needed.

DE.coverage: Full EU indication, assessed in three patient groups
DE.who: a1) women not treated before with a CDK4/6 inhibitor (neo)adjuvant; a2) women treated before with a CDK4/6 inhibitor (neo)adjuvant; b) men
DE.number: a) women (a1 + a2): about 860 to 3,590; b) men: about 8 to 35 patients
DE.number_note: patients in statutory health insurance (GKV), G-BA decision section 2
DE.conditions: PIK3CA mutation must be confirmed by a validated test
